input.strategy_title: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Public-sector deals require the model serving stack to run on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules. Today KServe
components and the serving data plane link non-validated crypto libraries in
several images, and we have no compliance evidence package. Certification
involves an external accredited laboratory (historical turnaround: six to nine
months) and mandatory security review board sign-off at defined milestones —
these human and third-party gates dominate the schedule regardless of
engineering speed.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | All serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters using validated crypto modules (no non-validated crypto in the request path). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A compliance evidence package (module inventory, build attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | CI enforces FIPS regressions: a gating check fails any serving-stack build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Platform Operator

## Out of Scope

- FIPS posture for workbenches, pipelines, and training (separate strategies)
- Common Criteria certification

## Open Questions

None on scope — but note that lab scheduling and review-board cadence are
externally controlled and cannot be compressed by engineering effort.

# FIPS remediation of KServe serving-stack images

## Description

This epic makes the KServe serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled
OpenShift clusters using validated cryptographic modules, with no non-validated
crypto in the request path. It delivers the remediated KServe images plus the
gating CI check that protects them against FIPS regressions.

## Scope

- Audit KServe serving-stack images to inventory the cryptographic libraries
  they link, identifying non-validated crypto in the request path (the audit
  output feeds the compliance module inventory).
- Rebuild/modify the KServe images so the request path uses validated
  cryptographic modules on FIPS-enabled clusters.
- Verify InferenceService request-path behavior (serving, and the deployment
  modes the stack supports) on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Author and verify the gating CI check covering KServe serving-stack builds:
  any build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage in these images must
  fail the check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A cryptographic audit of the KServe serving-stack images identifies every
  linked crypto library and its validation status; the request path shows no
  non-validated crypto.
- The remediated KServe images build and run correctly on a FIPS-enabled
  OpenShift cluster: an InferenceService successfully serves prediction
  requests end to end.
- The gating CI check runs on KServe serving-stack builds and fails a build
  that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (demonstrated with a
  deliberately non-compliant build).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules — KServe image share.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the FIPS regression CI check for KServe builds is
  authored and verified here rather than in a standalone enforcement epic; the
  check shares the same build surfaces this epic remediates, so splitting it
  would audit the same builds twice.

# FIPS remediation of Platform Operator images

## Description

This epic makes the Platform Operator images that form part of the serving data
plane run correctly on FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters using validated
cryptographic modules, with no non-validated crypto in the request path, plus
the gating CI check that protects those images against FIPS regressions.

## Scope

- Audit the Platform Operator images to inventory the cryptographic libraries
  they link, identifying non-validated crypto in the request path (the audit
  output feeds the compliance module inventory).
- Rebuild/modify the Platform Operator images so the request path uses
  validated cryptographic modules on FIPS-enabled clusters.
- Verify operator behavior (reconciliation and serving data plane lifecycle) on
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Author and verify the gating CI check covering Platform Operator builds: any
  build that reintroduces non-validated crypto usage in these images must fail
  the check.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A cryptographic audit of the Platform Operator images identifies every linked
  crypto library and its validation status; the request path shows no
  non-validated crypto.
- The remediated Platform Operator images build and run correctly on a
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift cluster, reconciling the serving data plane as
  expected.
- The gating CI check runs on Platform Operator builds and fails a build that
  reintroduces non-validated crypto usage (demonstrated with a deliberately
  non-compliant build).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): all serving-stack images run correctly on FIPS-enabled clusters
  using validated crypto modules — Platform Operator image share.
- HLR-3 (P1, bundled): the FIPS regression CI check for Platform Operator
  builds is authored and verified here rather than in a standalone enforcement
  epic; the check shares the same build surfaces this epic remediates, so
  splitting it would audit the same builds twice.

## Risks / Notes

- No architecture-context file exists for the Platform Operator component; its
  build pipeline status and dependencies are uncorroborated. If the component
  is not onboarded to a build pipeline, an onboarding chain must be added

# FIPS compliance evidence package and certification submission

## Description

This epic assembles the FIPS 140-3 compliance evidence package for the model
serving stack (module inventory, build attestations, test results) and
submits it through the security review board to the external accredited
certification laboratory.

## Scope

- Consolidate the module inventory: for every serving-stack image, the linked
  cryptographic modules and their validation status, drawing on the audits
  performed during the image remediation.
- Collect build attestations for the remediated serving-stack images,
  including the signed attestations produced by their build pipelines.
- Collect FIPS-mode test results demonstrating correct operation on
  FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- Assemble the package in the format required by the security review board and
  the certification lab, complete the board submission, and submit the package
  to the accredited lab.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The evidence package contains a module inventory covering every
  serving-stack image, with each linked crypto module's validation status
  recorded.
- The evidence package includes the build attestations produced by the
  serving-stack build pipelines, and those attestations validate.
- The evidence package includes FIPS-mode test results from FIPS-enabled
  clusters for the remediated images.
- The evidence package is submitted through the security review board and
  submitted to the external accredited certification lab, and its intake is
  confirmed.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a compliance evidence package (module inventory, build
  attestations, test results) is assembled and submitted through the security
  review board to the external certification lab.

## Risks / Notes

- Lab turnaround is historically six to nine months and the security review
  board meets on a fixed cadence; both are externally controlled and cannot be
  compressed by engineering effort. They are schedule risks, not acceptance
  criteria — the epic's controllable completion point is the assembled package
  and its confirmed submission/intake.

# Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites

## Description

This epic authors the user-facing documentation describing the model serving
stack's FIPS support posture and the cluster prerequisites for running it on
FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.

## Scope

- Author new documentation topics stating the FIPS support posture of the
  serving stack (what is supported, and its state relative to the certification
  submission) and the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled OpenShift
  clusters, including any required configuration.
- Where appropriate, include guidance on interpreting the compliance evidence
  for auditors and operators.
- Publish the topics through the Red Hat docs content process.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation states the serving stack's FIPS support posture and
  the cluster prerequisites for FIPS-enabled OpenShift clusters.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented FIPS
  remediation and the submitted evidence package, and review findings are
  addressed.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states the FIPS support posture and cluster
  prerequisites.

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9013

Strategy: FIPS 140-3 compliance for the model serving stack (Critical, Refinement Done).

## Triage Result

Neither Step 0 check fires. The strategy spans two components (KServe, Platform
Operator) and multiple distinct work streams (image remediation in two repos,
compliance evidence assembly with external certification submission, CI
enforcement, documentation), with HLRs at three priority levels. Proceeded to
full decomposition.

Affected Components list (KServe, Platform Operator — no change/owner columns),
out-of-scope list, and an open-questions note ("None on scope"). Missing
sections recorded as health warnings: no Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies
table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, no Non-Functional Requirements,
no Staff Engineer Input (Step 1.5 not applicable). Epic acceptance criteria are
therefore derived from the HLRs. Teams are inferred (see Health Warnings).

|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 | FIPS remediation of KServe serving-stack images | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 | FIPS remediation of Platform Operator images | Implementation | RHOAI Platform | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 | FIPS compliance evidence package and certification submission | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9013-E004 | Document the FIPS support posture and cluster prerequisites | Implementation | RHOAI Serving | P0 |

E004 carries `implementation_type: docs-authoring`. Its priority is P0 by the
docs-authoring priority exception (strategy frontmatter `priority: Critical`
→ P0), not by inheritance — see Health Warnings.

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001[RHAISTRAT-9013-E001 KServe FIPS remediation] --> E003[RHAISTRAT-9013-E003 Evidence package]
    E002[RHAISTRAT-9013-E002 Platform Operator FIPS remediation] --> E003
```

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 ∥ E002 (no edge) | Rule 14 | Different components in different repos with no shared artifacts; remediation of KServe images and Platform Operator images proceeds independently. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact consumer) | The evidence package's module inventory, build attestations, and test results are the deliverables of the remediated KServe builds; the package cannot be finalized until that remediation exists. The coupling to build-pipeline attestations is additionally expressed as an AC on E003 (evidence includes the attestations produced by the builds), not as an edge to any pipeline onboarding. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 13 (artifact consumer) | Same: the evidence package consumes the remediated Platform Operator build results as its content. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 11 | docs-authoring epic is blocked by all Implementation epics; docs describe what was built. |
| E002 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same. |
| E003 → E004 | Rule 11 | Same — the FIPS support posture documented must reflect the submitted evidence package, not a projected state. |

No Investigation epics: the strategy states "None on scope" for open
questions, and the remaining unknowns (which specific images/libraries link
non-validated crypto) are implementation details resolved by the audit each
remediation epic performs — the answer changes what changesets look like, not
which epics exist or what they deliver. The audit's output (module inventory)

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001, E002 | Split by component boundary: KServe images vs Platform Operator images; together they cover "all serving-stack images". |
| HLR-2 | P0 | E003 | Evidence package assembly and submission through the security review board to the external certification lab. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001, E002 (bundled) — the FIPS regression check is an enforcement deliverable over the same build surfaces the remediation converts; extracting it would be a standalone work-type epic auditing the same builds twice, so each remediation epic authors and verifies the gating check covering its own builds. | Shared-surface enforcement divided per surface (Rule on work-type extraction). |
